findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark theme preference
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-identical to light; body remains rgb(238,238,238), color-scheme is normal, and no prefers-color-scheme rule was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven surface/text colors.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences are not explicitly supported
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no forced-colors or prefers-contrast adaptation, while Lighthouse reports 3.49:1 navigation text contrast.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast treatment and ensure essential controls retain visible boundaries.

findings.summary: Route changes are abrupt full-document swaps
findings.evidence: The inspected MPA routes contain no cross-document View Transition rule or view-transition CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Use an opt-in cross-document View Transition for compatible same-origin navigation, retaining a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Page chrome does not communicate scroll position
findings.evidence: The 5,751px homepage and 8,518px listing have static header chrome and no scroll-state/progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a lightweight sticky-header state or progress affordance, respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long listing and detail navigation lacks attention cues
findings.evidence: The long mobile pages use abrupt jumps and conventional links without visible target highlighting or directional continuity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add target/focus highlighting and preserve focus when navigating to in-page states.

findings.summary: A full-screen consent wall obscures the primary content on every fresh visit
findings.evidence: All five representative page screenshots open behind a modal covering nearly the entire 360x800 viewport before any site task can begin.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the least intrusive legally compliant consent surface, reduce copy density, and avoid blocking non-personalized content.

findings.summary: Consent UI is a large custom div-based dialog
findings.evidence: DOM recon shows div.fc-dialog role=dialog rather than a native dialog; hidden preference dialogs add hundreds of headings to the document.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native dialog semantics where a modal is required and keep inactive preference content out of the accessibility tree.

findings.summary: Consent and advertising infrastructure dominate the content experience
findings.evidence: The first viewport is almost entirely consent chrome and the page loads 83 cross-origin requests for a compact editorial page.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize visible editorial content and defer non-essential ad/consent chrome until needed.

findings.summary: The mobile UI relies on a separate fixed mobile stylesheet rather than container-aware components
findings.evidence: Fetched mobile CSS contains no @container/container-type rules and 176 physical left/right declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Gradually isolate reusable cards/forms with container-type and logical sizing while retaining fallbacks.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible and many targets are undersized
findings.evidence: The focus probe reports outline-style none on the first 20 controls; multiple header/social targets are 21–33px high, below a comfortable touch target.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible style and expand compact controls to at least a comfortable 44px target area.

findings.summary: Cold-load LCP is slower than the good threshold
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.90s (performance 0.75), although the direct warm-ish trace measured 1.38s; this variability warrants optimization.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP content and defer ad/consent JavaScript from the critical path.

findings.summary: Third-party JavaScript dominates resource delivery
findings.evidence: HAR records 85 requests and 1.95MB transferred; scripts account for 1.40MB, including multiple 160–238KB advertising/tag bundles.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate, consolidate and defer third-party scripts; load only after consent/need and set useful cache policy.

findings.summary: Multiple overlapping advertising bundles dominate the page payload
findings.evidence: The largest resources are separate Prebid, OpenWrap, GPT, PageOS and Tag Manager bundles, while the core page is comparatively small.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate ad stacks and conditionally load the minimum vendor code needed for the chosen consent state.

findings.summary: Several prominent controls and objects have no accessible name
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility finds unnamed logo/login/register/social links and an object without alternate text.
findings.suggestedFix: Add discernible names to icon-only links and mark decorative embedded objects presentation-only or provide equivalent text.

findings.summary: Primary navigation text fails WCAG contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse/axe reports 3.49:1 for 14px #757575 navigation text on #e0e0e0, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken navigation text or adjust its surface to achieve at least 4.5:1.

findings.summary: Injected consent markup pollutes headings and focus is not visibly indicated
findings.evidence: DOM recon exposes hundreds of vendor names as H2 elements and several empty H1s; the focus probe reports no outline style.
findings.suggestedFix: Hide inactive vendor panels semantically, repair heading hierarchy, and add visible :focus-visible treatment.

findings.summary: The viewport prevents user zoom
findings.evidence: The viewport is maximum-scale=1/minimum-scale=1; Lighthouse explicitly fails the meta-viewport accessibility audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and minimum-scale restrictions and verify reflow at 200–400% zoom.

findings.summary: Image delivery lacks intrinsic dimensions and responsive sources
findings.evidence: The image probe found all 40 images missing width/height, 39 without srcset, and Lighthouse found incorrect aspect ratios/low-resolution images.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions/aspect-ratio and responsive srcset/sizes with appropriate-density sources.

findings.summary: Chrome reports unresolved platform issues
findings.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices is 0.69 and reports Inspector cookie issues plus third-party-cookie use.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve DevTools Issues, modernize cookie behavior, and test BFCache/deprecations after vendor cleanup.

findings.summary: Representative detail pages omit meta descriptions
findings.evidence: The product probe has no meta description, and discoverability reports null for the news article description, despite descriptive titles.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a unique summary meta description to each product, news and review template.

findings.summary: The sitemap endpoint is missing and AI/search agents are broadly blocked
findings.evidence: /sitemap.xml returns 404 and robots.txt blocks GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot and other agents.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a current sitemap and review crawler exclusions against the intended discovery policy.

findings.summary: Product and article templates lack structured/share metadata
findings.evidence: The product probe found zero JSON-LD blocks and zero Open Graph properties; article crawler evidence likewise shows no description.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Product/NewsArticle JSON-LD plus Open Graph/Twitter metadata matching visible content.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie flags are incomplete
findings.evidence: The HTTPS document lacks CSP, HSTS and nosniff; all five observed first-party cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Roll out CSP reporting/enforcement, HSTS and nosniff; set Secure and the narrowest appropriate SameSite value.

findings.summary: The page exposes users to an exceptionally broad advertising ecosystem
findings.evidence: The consent wall names 636 partners; the tracker run saw 18 third-party origins and four known trackers, and HAR attributes 1.94MB to cross-origin requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors and collected purposes, default to non-personalized delivery, and batch only necessary analytics after consent.

findings.summary: Available sign-in is password-only and lacks modern autocomplete/auth support
findings.evidence: The login form exposes email/password with autocomplete disabled; no passkey/WebAuthn affordance was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use correct username/current-password autocomplete now and add passkey sign-in/registration as an option.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are absent
findings.evidence: Headers evidence finds no HSTS, CSP/frame-ancestors on the document, X-Frame-Options, nosniff, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce the missing policies incrementally, beginning with HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking protection and a measured CSP rollout.

findings.summary: The installable-looking mobile site has no service worker/offline fallback
findings.evidence: A manifest exists, but the platform probe reports no service worker controller or registrations.
findings.suggestedFix: If installability is intended, add a minimal service worker and useful offline fallback; otherwise remove misleading app-capable signals.

findings.summary: The stylesheet is not writing-mode resilient
findings.evidence: HTML correctly declares lang=en, but CSS inspection found 176 physical left/right declarations and no sampled logical properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate layout spacing/positioning to inline/block logical properties and test RTL without changing content order.

findings.summary: Forms include unlabeled controls and cannot provide consistently understandable errors
findings.evidence: Phone Finder/login inspection shows email/password/search and many select fields without associated label text.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate visible labels and hints, validate after interaction, and announce errors in an aria-live summary.

findings.summary: Sign-in input assistance is disabled or missing
findings.evidence: The login email/password fields have empty autocomplete values and other controls explicitly use autocomplete=off.
findings.suggestedFix: Use email/username and current-password autocomplete tokens; keep autocomplete enabled unless there is a specific risk.

findings.summary: Images use legacy formats without responsive delivery
findings.evidence: All 40 homepage images are legacy GIF/JPEG, 39 lack srcset and 33 below-fold images are not lazy loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP variants, add srcset/sizes and lazy-load below-fold images while prioritizing the LCP image.

findings.summary: Advertising work consumes most transferred bytes without supporting the core reading task
findings.evidence: HAR shows 1.40MB of scripts and 83 cross-origin requests, dominated by several ad bidding/vendor bundles.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate redundant vendors and only fetch advertising code after the relevant consent and viewport need.

findings.summary: Third-party resource use is disproportionate to the compact page
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 1.94MB of the 1.95MB transfer; fonts consume 143KB and advertising scripts are the largest assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget and enforce it per consent state.

findings.summary: Public reference content is not intentionally agent-readable
findings.evidence: Pages are server-rendered (72–78% raw-content coverage), but key AI crawlers are blocked and no structured Product/NewsArticle data or agent surface was found.
findings.suggestedFix: If agent discovery is desired, allow selected crawlers and expose accurate structured data or read-only agent capabilities.
